household.title: manioc-sifter; tray

household.name: maniokpress, press
household.title: maniokpress, press
household.reason: This is a woven tipiti (manioc/cassava press), a braided cylindrical basketry tool used to squeeze toxic juice from grated cassava, documented as made and named by the Wapishana at Sand Creek, Guyana in 1962.

household.name: basket
household.title: basket
household.reason: A finely woven child's basket with feather decoration, consistent with Wapishana basketry traditions of the Guiana region; museum attributes it directly to the Wapishana.

household.name: manioc-squeezer
household.title: manioc-squeezer
household.reason: This is a classic tipiti (basketry manioc squeezer), a well-documented Wapishana/Guiana craft item made from woven fibre and decorated with feathers, matching both the claimed ethnicity and household category.

household.name: modell, maniokpress
household.title: modell, maniokpress
household.reason: The image shows a woven plaited-fiber model of a tipiti (manioc press), a household tool used by Wapishana and other Guiana groups for processing manioc; consistent with the museum's own description.

household.name: sikt
household.title: sikt
household.reason: The image shows a woven basketry sieve/tray (sikt = sieve in Swedish), a traditional manioc-processing tool collected among the Taruma and Wapishana of British Guiana by Walter Roth in 1927 — a plausible household item for this people.

household.name: back-pack; basket
